source.title: Circuit-Tracer: A New Library for Finding Feature Circuits
source.authors: Michael P. Hanna; Mateusz Piotrowski; Jack W Lindsey; E. Ameisen

record.tranche_reason: The paper applies transcoder feature tracing and interventions to Gemma-2 (2B), reporting case studies that bear on whether sparse dictionary features in an LLM can be identified and affect outputs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports two feature-intervention case studies relevant to V4. Background statements about polysemanticity and sparse dictionaries, cited findings from other work, and intervention settings chosen by the authors are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: A software paper for the circuit-tracer library. It treats transcoder features as a given tool. Its two case studies only show the library reproducing prior circuit findings (Dallas→Texas→Austin; separate language and concept features). It does not test whether features are superposed, spread across neurons, or recoverable by a dictionary as a claim about the model.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors present circuit-tracer as a library for finding, visualizing, annotating and intervening on transcoder feature circuits (up to 14B models). They say the case studies demonstrate its ability to reproduce existing results.
record.recipe_differences: Uses transcoder feature-circuit attribution and activation interventions in an LLM; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Interventions on manually identified transcoder features in Gemma-2 (2B) shift outputs: Austin to Sacramento in Figure 3, and Spanish to English continuation in Figure 4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transcoder-feature circuits identify causally relevant intermediate features in LLMs (circuit-tracing validity, not superposition).

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 8th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: Evidence consists of two illustrative case studies on one model, without reported uncertainty or controls. Feature identification and annotation are manual. The Texas intervention description is inconsistent about whether the features were upweighted or downweighted.

untested.parts: No test of capacity causes of polysemanticity.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
Transcoder features are used as a tool. There is no measure of feature spread across neurons, and no evaluation of dictionary recovery (reconstruction, interpretability rates).
No test of the completeness, stability or canonicity of features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label is removed. The study is a tool/demo paper that relies on dictionary features rather than testing V4. The background mention of polysemanticity due to capacity pressure cites Elhage et al. (2022) only.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network experiment tests superposition geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
No experiment tests whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
No experiment tests alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Tests transcoder features in two case studies on Gemma-2 (2B); does not test feature spread across neurons, SAE recovery specifically, or other models.
No test of whether dictionary features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
No test of whether the represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 (2B)
rows.operation_detail: Constrained feature intervention at the Dallas position: Texas feature activations multiplied by 4 and California feature activations set to 10 times their original value.

conditions.value: Fact: The capital of the state containing Dallas is

rows.measure: Next-token output distribution; reported top-token probabilities
rows.baseline: Figure only; Austin 0.441, not 0.077, Texas 0.053, Fort 0.041, Hecho 0.036
rows.value: Figure only; Sacramento 0.303, Austin 0.112, not 0.087, the 0.077, San 0.041
rows.note: The text describes a shift from Austin to Sacramento after intervention. It calls the Texas features downweighted but says their activations were multiplied by 4; the report is internally inconsistent about the direction of that edit.
rows.check: This is a feature-steering demo of the tool (multi-hop state representation), not a measure of superposition or of dictionary recoverability. The Figure 3 title reads 'The state containing Dallas has its capital in', which differs from the prompt in the text. Texas features are 'multiplied by 4' while also described as downweighted and, in the caption, 'ablated'; a minus sign is likely missing.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 (2B)
rows.operation_detail: Open-ended intervention setting Spanish feature activations to -2 times their original value at all non-BOS positions.
rows.value: Intervened generation continues with English-language text
rows.note: The authors identify distinct basketball/sports and Spanish features and pathways; the reported intervention changes the continuation language.
rows.check: This is a tool demo (ablating Spanish features at -2x changes the output language). It reproduces a cited result and does not measure superposition or feature recovery. It is also a single sampled continuation with no controls.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2 (2B), the two reported case-study prompts
reader_labels.reason: The authors identify transcoder features and report output changes after intervening on them, supporting recoverable, causally relevant dictionary features in these examples (r1, r2).
